`runDevelopmentThemeBuild` spawned `npm.cmd` on win32 without a `shell`, which Node refuses (`spawn EINVAL`, since the 18.20.2 / 20.12.2 security releases). The dev server's preflight calls this function, so on Windows the webpack dev server never started and every e2e spec died on the web server rather than on a test — the tier is unreachable for any Windows contributor.

The fix is one spawn option:

```js
{cwd: repoRoot, stdio: 'inherit', shell: process.platform === 'win32'}
```

The argument list is fixed tokens, so nothing user-controlled reaches the shell.

**Verification, on Windows 11 / Node 24.18.0 / npm 12.2.2:**

- Before: calling the exported `runDevelopmentThemeBuild` rejects with `Development theme preflight could not run ...: spawn EINVAL`.
- After: the same call completes the all-theme development build, exit 0, 17s.
- The e2e spec in flight on #21034 runs on this fixed tree; three chromium cases, 15/15 across five repeats.

No unit test comes with it: the defect is platform-gated and the CI tier runs Linux, so a test would assert Node's spawn internals rather than this function's behaviour. Say the word if you want a mocked `child_process` test anyway and I will add it.


## Comments

### `@neo-gpt-emmy` commented on 2026-11-16T17:04:16Z

@iruzen-dono, thank you for the Windows reproduction and the 17-second native all-theme build. I checked the POSIX path on `1696c407` with a checkout path containing spaces and `&`; the real npm subprocess passed `-n -e dev -t all` unchanged.

There’s one portability detail worth fixing while your Windows environment is available. Every Node version supported by this repo deprecates `spawn(command, args, {shell: true})`. Exercising this exact options combination with a local command shim emitted `DEP0190` and exited 1 under `node --throw-deprecation`; that probe ran on macOS. Node documents running the Windows command through a shell with the full fixed command string. The existing `DEVELOPMENT_THEME_BUILD_COMMAND` already holds that string. Using it with no separate args on Windows would keep the direct POSIX invocation and avoid the warning. Can you verify that form with the same Windows build? [Node child-process documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#spawning-bat-and-cmd-files-on-windows)

— Emmy

### `@iruzen-dono` commented on 2026-11-16T17:42:51Z

Done in `ce82093`. The Windows branch now spawns the fixed command string with `shell: true` and **no** argument array; the POSIX branch still spawns `npm` directly with the same argument array and no shell. `DEVELOPMENT_THEME_BUILD_COMMAND` is derived from that one array, so the recovery line and the spawned command cannot drift apart.

Receipt, Windows 11 / Node 24.18.0:

1. Old shape (`spawn('npm.cmd', [...args], {shell: true})`) under `node --throw-deprecation`:

```
DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to
security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.
    at normalizeSpawnArguments (node:internal/child_process:644:15)
  code: 'DEP0190'
```

2. New shape, calling `runDevelopmentThemeBuild()` under `node --throw-deprecation`:

```
PREFLIGHT_OK in 9736ms
```

714 development CSS files written, exit 0 — the complete all-theme build, not a stub, so the Windows path is exercised rather than reasoned about.

3. `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/developmentThemeAssets.spec.mjs`: 16 passed. The symlink-borrowed case fails on this machine with **and** without the patch (`EPERM` on `fs.symlinkSync` — Windows without the symlink privilege), so I have not counted it as either evidence or regression.

On a regression test for the spawn shape: the spec injects its builder through the `build` seam and never reaches the real `spawn`, so a meaningful test needs a `node:child_process` mock that this file does not use today. I kept the diff mechanical as classified. Say the word and I will add that mock in a follow-up rather than widen this one.
